n: Back in Kirtland in late August 1831, the Saints were eager to hear about Zion. The Lord calls everyone who claims to be his people to open their hearts and hear his will.
This is the voice of the One whose anger burns against the wicked and rebellious.
He decides who is taken in death and who is preserved in life. Life and death are in his hands.

f.w: take even them whom he will take

n: He builds and destroys at his will and has power to cast the soul into hell. Jesus taught that we should fear God rather than people.

f.w: able to cast the soul down to hell

n: When the Lord speaks, his word will be obeyed.

f.w: I, the Lord, utter my voice

n: The wicked should take heed, the rebellious tremble, and unbelievers stop scoffing, for wrath will come like a whirlwind and all will know he is God.

f.g: Keep quiet; stop speaking against God.

n: Those who seek signs will see them—but signs alone will not save them.
Some among the Saints seek signs, as people have from the beginning. Ezra Booth, for one, had joined after seeing a healing and later left in disappointment.
A key principle: faith does not come from signs; signs follow those who believe.
Signs come by faith and according to God’s will—not on human demand.

f.w: not by the will of men

n: Signs and mighty works flow from faith, for without faith no one pleases God. To those he is displeased with, he shows signs only in judgment.

f.w: without faith no man pleaseth God

n: The Lord is displeased with those who seek signs to build their faith rather than to bless others and glorify God.
He gives commandments, yet many have turned away from them.
There were adulterers and adulteresses among the Saints; some have left, and others still among them will be exposed.
Let them repent quickly, before judgment catches them like a trap and their foolishness becomes public.
Lust and adultery in the heart drive away the Spirit, lead to denying the faith, and bring fear. Moral purity and spiritual strength are tied together.

f.w: he that looketh on a woman to lust after her

n: Echoing Revelation, the Lord lists those who face the “second death”—spiritual separation from God: the fearful, unbelievers, liars, the sexually immoral, and sorcerers.

f.w: that lake which burneth with fire and brimstone, which is the second death

n: Such people will not rise in the first resurrection, which is for the righteous.
The Church as a whole is not justified while these sins remain among them.
But whoever endures in faith and does God’s will will overcome and inherit the earth in the day of transfiguration.

f.g: When the earth is renewed and glorified at Christ’s coming.

n: The earth will be transfigured in a way shown to Peter, James, and John on the Mount of Transfiguration—though the full account has not yet been revealed.

f.w: the pattern which was shown unto mine apostles upon the mount

n: The Lord will make his will known—not as a commandment, since many ignore commandments.
To those who keep his commandments, he reveals the mysteries of his kingdom, which become a well of living water springing up to eternal life.

f.w: a well of living water, springing up unto everlasting life

n: The Saints are to gather to Zion—but not in haste, which brings confusion and disease.
The Lord holds the land of Zion in his own hands.

f.w: I, the Lord, hold it in mine own hands

n: Yet he renders to Caesar what is Caesar’s—respecting civil law and property rights.

f.w: render unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar's

n: So the Saints must buy the land, giving them a legal claim and avoiding provoking their neighbors.

f.w: that you may have advantage of the world
f.g: Here, a lawful standing or claim in the eyes of the world.

n: Satan stirs people’s hearts to anger and bloodshed against them.
Zion can be obtained only by purchase or by blood.
If by purchase, the Saints are blessed.
If by blood—which they are forbidden to shed—their enemies will drive them from city to city, and few will remain. This sadly anticipated their expulsion from Jackson County in 1833.
The Lord is angry with the wicked and is withdrawing his Spirit from the earth’s inhabitants.
He has decreed wars on the earth—the wicked will kill the wicked, and fear will grip everyone.

f.w: the wicked shall slay the wicked

n: The Saints will barely escape, but the Lord will be with them and come down from his Father’s presence to destroy the wicked.

f.w: the saints also shall hardly escape

n: This is not yet—but it will come.
Because these judgments are coming, the Lord wants his Saints gathered in Zion.
Every person should hold righteousness in his hands, wear faithfulness like a belt, and warn the world—by words and even by leaving—that desolation is coming.
The disciples in Kirtland living on “this farm”—the Isaac Morley farm—should arrange their affairs.

f.g: Isaac Morley’s farm near Kirtland, where many Saints had settled and lived communally.

n: Titus Billings, who manages the farm, should sell the land and prepare to move to Zion in spring with its residents, except those the Lord keeps back.

f.g: An early convert and Isaac Morley’s brother-in-law; he led a company to Missouri in 1832.

n: All money that can be spared, whether little or much, should be sent to Zion.
Joseph Smith will be given power to discern by the Spirit who should go to Zion and who should stay.
Newel K. Whitney should keep his store for a little while.

f.g: A Kirtland merchant; his store became an important Church center.

n: But he should send all the money he can to Zion.
These things are in his hands; he should act wisely.
He is to be appointed as an agent for the disciples who remain in Kirtland.
He and Oliver Cowdery should visit the branches quickly, explaining these things and raising funds.
Those who are faithful and endure will overcome the world.
Those who send treasures to Zion will receive an inheritance here and a reward in the world to come.
Blessed are those who die in the Lord: at his coming, when all things become new, they will rise, never die again, and receive an inheritance in the holy city.

f.w: blessed are the dead that die in the Lord

n: Those alive at his coming who kept the faith are blessed, yet they will still “die” at an advanced age.
During the Millennium, children will grow old, and the old will be changed in an instant from mortality to immortality rather than lying in the grave.

f.w: changed in the twinkling of an eye

n: This is why the apostles preached the resurrection.
Speaking in the Lord’s way of time, these things are near and will come at the Son of Man’s coming.

f.w: speaking after the manner of the Lord
f.g: Measured by God’s timeframe, not ours.

n: Until then, foolish virgins will live among the wise; at his coming, the righteous and wicked will be fully separated.
The Lord is displeased with Sidney Rigdon: he became proud, rejected counsel, and grieved the Spirit.
So his description of Zion is unacceptable; he must write another, or lose his office.
Those who meekly desire to warn sinners may be ordained to do so.
This is a day of warning, not of many words. God will not be mocked in the last days.
The Lord is above all and his power reaches beneath; he is over, in, and through all things, and searches everything.

f.w: over all, and in all, and through all

n: He identifies himself: Alpha and Omega, Jesus Christ.
Therefore, people should be careful how they speak his name.
Many are condemned for using the Lord’s name in vain—speaking or acting in it without authority.
The Church must repent, and the Lord will claim them as his own; otherwise they will be cut off.
What comes from heaven is sacred and must be spoken carefully, under the Spirit’s direction, which comes through prayer. Without that, there is condemnation.

f.g: When the Spirit prompts or compels.

f.w: that which cometh from above is sacred

n: Joseph and Sidney should seek homes, as the Spirit teaches through prayer. They soon moved to Hiram, Ohio.
These challenges are to be overcome through patience, bringing a “more exceeding and eternal weight of glory”—or greater condemnation if not.

f.w: a more exceeding and eternal weight of glory
